We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=27{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=54x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 27{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(27{x}^{2})(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})(54x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-9{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+18\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})\cdot 1\,dx \\  & =\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{9}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 27{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =-9{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+18\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-9{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+18(\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{9}+D) \\  & =-9{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=18D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}27{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={[-9{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)]}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =9{(\frac{\pi }{3})}^{2}-2-2 \\  & ={\pi }^{2}-4 \\  & ={\pi }^{2}-4\end{aligned}
$$
